slot.brief: Figure shows a cyclic or branched alkene; predict the carbonyl fragments obtained on reductive ozonolysis.

stem: The alkene shown in the figure is treated with $\text{O}_3$, followed by $\text{Zn}/\text{H}_2\text{O}$. Which carbonyl product is formed?

verdicts.working: Reductive ozonolysis cleaves the ring alkene. The alkene carbon bearing the methyl group forms a ketone; the other, bearing H, forms an aldehyde. The product is OHC–(CH₂)₄–CO–CH₃, or 6-oxoheptanal.

working:
Cleavage of the ring C=C gives a ketone at the methyl-substituted carbon and an aldehyde at the carbon bearing H.
Product: $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}(\text{CH}_2)_4\text{CHO}$ = 6-oxoheptanal.

Independent check: Reductive ozonolysis cleaves the ring alkene. The alkene carbon bearing the methyl group forms a ketone; the other, bearing H, forms an aldehyde. The product is OHC–(CH₂)₄–CO–CH₃, or 6-oxoheptanal.
solution:
Reductive ozonolysis cleaves the ring C=C: the methyl-substituted carbon forms a ketone, while the carbon bearing H forms an aldehyde.
$$\mathrm{OHC-(CH_2)_4-CO-CH_3}$$
This is 6-oxoheptanal.

figure.description: Draw the skeletal structure of 1-methylcyclohex-1-ene: a six-membered ring with one C=C bond; attach a methyl group to one of the two alkene carbons. All other ring bonds are single bonds.

draft.working:
Cleavage of the ring C=C gives a ketone at the methyl-substituted carbon and an aldehyde at the carbon bearing H.
Product: $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}(\text{CH}_2)_4\text{CHO}$ = 6-oxoheptanal.
draft.distractor_notes:
B: treats both alkene carbons as aldehyde carbons and loses the methyl substituent.
C: gives the ketone–aldehyde chain one carbon too short.
D: incorrectly retains the methyl group as a branch and forms a dialdehyde.
